text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Singapore Home Affairs Minister Wong Kan Seng says Polling Day is likely to be announced by noon on Monday.
- Peruvian rebels threaten to kill Japanese diplomat and release five diplomats to negotiate with the government.
- Japan's Imperial Household Agency announces cancellation of all celebrations for Emperor Akihito's birthday.
- Four Singapore Democratic Party members pay contempt fines hours before one-week deadline.
- Singapore government releases last two commercial land parcels for this year.
- OECD says economic activity to remain subdued in short term in the dynamic Asian economies due to slower export growth and tight money policies.
- English Premier League football club Newcastle United confirms plans for British stock market flotation.

- Negotiations begins between Singapore Telecom and major U.S. telecommunications carriers on cost of long-distance calls and may result in lower Singapore Telecom profits due to lower IDD rates for consumers.
- Shenzhen branch of Guangdong International Trust and Investment Corp to set up company here to manage overseas operations.
- Stock Exchange of Thailand delays by six months implementation of stricter rules on forced selling.
- Shenyin and Wanguo Securities abort plans for Hong Kong-based fund management joint venture with Singapore firm.
- Retail-based Transmarco's net profit down by 77 percent to Singapore $275,000 for six months to September 30.
- Sembawang Corp hits out at DBS research unit over report.
- WBL Corporation Ltd records net earnings to Singapore $32.95 million on 2.6 percent turnover growth to $751.44 million for year ended September 30.
- Net earnings of Wearnes International up 4.6 percent to Singapore $19.28 million.
